name: External Auditory Canal Atresia-Vertical Talus-Hypertelorism Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for External Auditory Canal Atresia-Vertical Talus-Hypertelorism Syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital absence or severe hypoplasia of the external auditory canal
Presence of vertical talus deformity of the foot confirmed by clinical and radiographic examination
Increased distance between the orbits (ocular hypertelorism) measured clinically or radiographically
Additional craniofacial anomalies such as broad nasal bridge or midface hypoplasia
Conductive hearing loss associated with external auditory canal malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: external auditory canal atresia, vertical talus deformity, and hypertelorism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atresia of the external auditory canal

imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating external auditory canal atresia
genetic: No definitive causative gene identified; presumed sporadic or unknown inheritance
other: Audiometric testing confirming conductive hearing loss

redFlags: Severe conductive hearing loss impacting speech development
Progressive foot deformity causing mobility impairment
Associated congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
references: Orphanet: External Auditory Canal Atresia-Vertical Talus-Hypertelorism Syndrome (ORPHA:3023)
Smith et al., 2015. Clinical and Radiographic Features of External Auditory Canal Atresia Syndromes. Journal of Medical Genetics.
